answer: Bonded attestation blocks sybils: an agent must lock collateral before its votes are counted, and any duplicate or collusive signature lets peers slash that bond. An attacker can mint a nebula of throwaway identities, but each needs its own deposit, so influence is priced in capital, not in key generation. Weight climbs to a useful summit only after a long clean history, and the only inlet for new weight is fresh collateral, so every fake identity costs per head and is burned on detection.
